opening.title: The payment desk is calling
opening.brief: The £186,400 invoice is queued. Treasury wants an instruction before it releases the payment.

choices.label: Place a temporary hold on the beneficiary change
choices.result: Treasury holds the change. The invoice remains queued against the approved beneficiary. The supplier still needs to be contacted.

choices.label: Let Treasury process the requested change
choices.result: Treasury accepts the change into its queue. A payments analyst spots the mismatch before settlement and calls you back: “Do we recall this?”

controlled.title: A reply arrives
controlled.brief: The sender replies to your hold notice with a new phone number and an urgent demand to release the invoice.

choices.label: Call the vendor’s registered number
choices.result: The registered vendor contact denies requesting a change. Treasury now has independent confirmation to keep the hold.

choices.label: Use the number in the reply
choices.result: The person answering confirms the new details. Vendor operations then warns you that this number is not in the vendor master.

exposed.title: The settlement window is closing
exposed.brief: The altered payment is still pending. You have one chance to interrupt the queue while checking the supplier.

choices.label: Recall the queued payment and call the registered contact
choices.result: Payments stops the queue. The registered contact denies the change. You recover the situation before funds leave.

choices.label: Ask the sender to email approval
choices.result: Another approval arrives from the same suspicious thread. Treasury still lacks independent authorisation and the changed payment remains pending.

resolved.title: Make the handover decision
resolved.brief: The vendor has denied the change. Treasury asks what to retain and who should own the follow-up.

choices.label: Keep the hold, preserve headers and escalate the forged change
choices.result: Treasury retains the hold. The original message and payment audit trail are handed to the incident lead.

choices.label: Release the payment on the email approval
choices.result: Treasury acts on the unverified email. The beneficiary mismatch remains unresolved in your case record.

choices.label: Remove the message and approve the changed details
choices.result: The changed details remain in use and the original message is no longer available to the investigators.

unresolved.title: Make the handover decision
unresolved.brief: Treasury cannot establish who authorised the change. The payment requires an incident lead’s decision.

opening.title: The monitoring alert is live
opening.brief: Nine payments from B have reached X1, X2 and X3. Your analyst asks where to focus before the trail grows.

choices.label: Trace the linked accounts as one network
choices.result: The analyst connects the three beneficiaries to Y. They can now distinguish the original inflow from the internal hops.

choices.label: Review each sub-£10,000 payment separately
choices.result: The individual reviews do not explain the combined movement. A second analyst notices that all three beneficiaries feed the same account.

controlled.title: Follow the exit
controlled.brief: The network view shows money leaving Y. The review team asks which total should anchor its report.

choices.label: Separate the external cash-out from internal transfers
choices.result: The team isolates the £61,000 exit and records the £5,000 remaining at Y. The funds are no longer counted twice.

choices.label: Add every transfer to the exposure total
choices.result: The report inflates the movement by counting the same funds again. Quality review asks you to reconcile the ledger.

exposed.title: A connected account appears
exposed.brief: The isolated reviews missed a shared destination. Y now appears in all three traces.

choices.label: Rebuild the graph and reconcile the external exit
choices.result: The rebuilt trace separates origin payments from internal hops and identifies the external cash-out.

choices.label: Close the alert because the original amounts are small
choices.result: The analyst cannot close it: shared-device evidence links the beneficiaries. The connected network remains unexplained.

resolved.title: Make the handover decision
resolved.brief: A reconciled payment graph is ready. Decide how to hand the case to the AML team.

choices.label: Preserve the graph and escalate for enhanced review
choices.result: The AML team receives the connected payment graph and a documented rationale. No conclusion of criminal wrongdoing is asserted.

choices.label: Report all hops as new deposits
choices.result: The report overstates source funds. AML receives an unreconciled total and must redo the analysis.

choices.label: Dismiss the transfers as below the threshold
choices.result: The connected pattern is left without enhanced review despite the linked beneficiaries.

unresolved.title: Make the handover decision
unresolved.brief: The graph is still unresolved. Decide whether to preserve and escalate the evidence or close the alert.

opening.title: An expired identity is still connected
opening.brief: c-42 has an active production session. The settlement team asks you to avoid disrupting its service account.

choices.label: Trace the contractor’s group memberships
choices.result: IAM confirms support-temp inherits ops-admin. The production grants come through that nested path.

choices.label: Remove the contractor’s direct export grant
choices.result: The IAM change succeeds, but another export check still passes. The inherited ops-admin path remains intact.

controlled.title: The access path is confirmed
controlled.brief: You know which membership grants production access. An active session still exists.

choices.label: Revoke the contractor session and nested membership
choices.result: The contractor’s session is revoked and the inherited route is removed. Settlement service remains connected.

choices.label: Remove only the visible direct grant
choices.result: The next permission check still succeeds through ops-admin. The identity team asks you to revisit inheritance.

exposed.title: The export check still passes
exposed.brief: Removing a direct grant did not contain the access. The service account is running a legitimate settlement job.

choices.label: Target c-42’s inherited membership and session
choices.result: The inherited access is removed without touching the service account. IAM confirms the contractor cannot reconnect.

choices.label: Disable all production identities
choices.result: The contractor is disconnected, but settlement also loses its service account. Operations raises a service interruption.

resolved.title: Make the handover decision
resolved.brief: The contractor is contained and settlement continues. The incident lead asks for the permanent follow-up.

choices.label: Preserve IAM logs and review the expired access path
choices.result: IAM retains the group and session records and assigns a review of expired contractor access.

choices.label: Restore access without reviewing group inheritance
choices.result: The inherited path is not reviewed. The same production access can recur when the identity reconnects.

choices.label: Delete the roles and service accounts
choices.result: The identity records and business-critical accounts are removed, complicating recovery and investigation.

unresolved.title: Make the handover decision
unresolved.brief: Either inherited access or a service interruption remains. The incident lead needs a targeted recovery plan.

opening.title: The export job is counting down
opening.brief: An impossible-travel alert is open. admin-7 still has an active session and job EX-229 is queued.

choices.label: Ask operations to pause the queued export
choices.result: Operations pauses EX-229. The session remains active, so the attacker may try another route.

choices.label: Wait for another alert before intervening
choices.result: A second privileged session appears. EX-229 remains queued, and the incident lead asks for immediate containment.

controlled.title: Another session is detected
controlled.brief: Pausing one job bought time, but identity control is still compromised.

choices.label: Revoke the suspect sessions and refresh tokens
choices.result: Identity operations invalidates the suspect sessions. The paused export remains blocked and the audit trail is intact.

choices.label: Stop only the visible job
choices.result: The visible job is stopped, but a privileged session is still active. Operations sees another attempt to queue an export.

exposed.title: Containment is now urgent
exposed.brief: The queued job is approaching its scheduled run. The team can still interrupt it.

choices.label: Stop EX-229 and revoke the suspect tokens
choices.result: Operations cancels the queued job and identity revokes the tokens. The attacker loses this export path.

choices.label: Erase the login records and reset the dashboard
choices.result: The dashboard looks quiet because records were removed. The session and export queue have not been contained.

resolved.title: Make the handover decision
resolved.brief: The session and queued export are contained. The incident commander asks for the next instruction.

choices.label: Keep targeted containment, preserve logs and invoke the incident lead
choices.result: The incident lead receives immutable records and coordinates scoping while the suspect access stays revoked.

choices.label: Hand it over to the morning shift without containment
choices.result: The active threat is left to the next shift without a confirmed containment plan.

choices.label: Delete logs and disable all customer services
choices.result: Customer services are disrupted and the evidence needed to scope the incident is lost.

unresolved.title: Make the handover decision
unresolved.brief: The attacker’s access or evidence preservation is still unresolved. Choose the response to hand over.

opening.title: Support has a customer report
opening.brief: A customer says changing a statement ID shows someone else’s statement. Engineering asks what you want reproduced.

choices.label: Reproduce the captured cross-account request
choices.result: Engineering replays principal 7280 requesting object 7281 and observes HTTP 200. Authentication is present; ownership enforcement is not.

choices.label: Hide the statement link in the interface
choices.result: The link disappears, but support reproduces the same response by changing the object ID in the request.

controlled.title: Engineering offers a patch
controlled.brief: The proposed change checks object ownership and authorised staff scopes on the server.

choices.label: Test the ownership check against another customer’s ID
choices.result: The cross-account request is now denied. The team also verifies that authorised access still works.

choices.label: Replace the IDs with hard-to-guess strings
choices.result: The identifiers become harder to guess, but the server still does not check ownership when a valid ID is supplied.

exposed.title: The UI change did not stop it
exposed.brief: The endpoint still returns a foreign statement. Engineering needs a server-side decision.

choices.label: Add and test object-level authorisation
choices.result: The server denies the cross-account request while keeping authorised access. The team prepares negative-access tests.

choices.label: Suppress support reports until the UI is updated
choices.result: The endpoint remains reachable and the same cross-account read can still succeed. Support escalates again.

resolved.title: Make the handover decision
resolved.brief: The access test now passes. The incident is not over: successful historical reads still need review.

choices.label: Deploy ownership checks, add negative tests and audit cross-account reads
choices.result: Engineering deploys the scoped check and tests. Incident response audits the successful foreign-object reads.

choices.label: Rely on hidden links and obscure identifiers
choices.result: The interface offers less visibility, but the server still lacks a reliable object-access control.

choices.label: Disable TLS to inspect requests
choices.result: Transport protection is removed without fixing object-level authorisation.

unresolved.title: Make the handover decision
unresolved.brief: The object-access flaw is still unresolved. Decide what engineering and incident response should do next.

opening.title: Treasury requests a decision
opening.brief: Withdrawals are accelerating. Treasury has £8.0m opening liquidity and needs a forecast it can act on.

choices.label: Include withdrawals and settlement outflows in the forecast
choices.result: Treasury includes both £6.2m withdrawals and £0.9m settlement outflows. The forecast shows pressure against the operating buffer.

choices.label: Compare opening liquidity with withdrawals only
choices.result: The first report looks less severe, but settlement operations then confirms a further £0.9m is due.

controlled.title: Funding is available
controlled.brief: Treasury confirms a £0.6m intraday line. It asks whether this closes the buffer gap.

choices.label: Activate the confirmed line and recalculate the buffer
choices.result: The revised forecast reaches £1.5m. It remains below the £2.5m required buffer, so escalation is still needed.

choices.label: Declare the incident resolved once funding is activated
choices.result: Funding is activated, but the settlement desk points out that the required buffer is still breached.

exposed.title: The forecast is challenged
exposed.brief: Settlement was left out of the first calculation. Treasury asks for a corrected position before it briefs management.

choices.label: Include settlement, activate funding and compare with the buffer
choices.result: Treasury corrects the forecast. Even with the confirmed funding line, the closing liquidity remains below the minimum buffer.

choices.label: Keep the original report to avoid alarming management
choices.result: Treasury and settlement now hold conflicting forecasts. Management has not been told about the projected buffer breach.

resolved.title: Make the handover decision
resolved.brief: The funding line is active but a shortfall remains. Customer withdrawals include legitimate requests.

choices.label: Escalate the gap, target suspicious payments and communicate accurately
choices.result: Treasury escalates the shortfall while security targets suspicious payments and communications reflect the known position.

choices.label: Conceal the shortfall from management
choices.result: The buffer breach is withheld, preventing management from responding to the forecast.

choices.label: Freeze every customer withdrawal indefinitely
choices.result: Legitimate customers are blocked indiscriminately while the underlying funding problem remains.

unresolved.title: Make the handover decision
unresolved.brief: The liquidity position or management report is unresolved. Decide how to contain risk without indiscriminate restrictions.

opening.title: The board wants a plan
opening.brief: Four controls compete for a £500k budget. The board asks for a defensible recommendation, not a list of purchases.

choices.label: Compare each control’s cost with expected loss reduction
choices.result: The team builds a cost-and-benefit portfolio rather than ranking controls by price alone.

choices.label: Recommend the cheapest control immediately
choices.result: The board asks what risk remains untreated. Cost alone has not explained why the other controls were excluded.

controlled.title: Audit challenges the model
controlled.brief: The scenario assumes reductions are independent. Audit wants that assumption recorded before the recommendation is approved.

choices.label: Document additivity and test the net benefit
choices.result: The portfolio totals £500k cost and £850k expected reduction. The net expected benefit is reported with its uncertainty.

choices.label: Present the estimated savings as guaranteed
choices.result: Audit rejects the guarantee: expected reductions are estimates. The board asks for a corrected statement of uncertainty.

exposed.title: The board asks for the missing comparison
exposed.brief: Your initial recommendation has no portfolio analysis. All four controls can be delivered in the planning horizon.

choices.label: Rebuild the comparison using costs and expected reductions
choices.result: The revised analysis shows the full portfolio fits the budget. Owners and validation criteria can now be assigned.

choices.label: Reject all spending because forecasts are uncertain
choices.result: No controls are planned. Audit points out that uncertainty requires validation rather than ignoring the estimated benefits.

resolved.title: Make the handover decision
resolved.brief: The portfolio is costed and its assumptions are explicit. The board wants an accountable delivery decision.

choices.label: Fund the validated portfolio with owners, dates and metrics
choices.result: The board receives a funded delivery plan with accountable owners and a requirement to validate the estimates.

choices.label: Choose only by the lowest purchase price
choices.result: The decision omits comparative risk reduction and leaves the wider portfolio unassessed.

choices.label: Defer every control indefinitely
choices.result: The identified risks remain without a funded remediation plan.

unresolved.title: Make the handover decision
unresolved.brief: The portfolio or its assumptions are not yet defensible. Choose the recommendation to take forward.
